    AI Overview
    Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic inflammatory skin condition causing painful, recurring lumps, abscesses, and tunnels under the skin, usually in areas where skin rubs together (armpits, groin). Caused by clogged hair follicles, it is not contagious or caused by poor hygiene. Treatment includes medications (antibiotics, biologics, steroids) and surgery. 
    Symptoms and Stages 
    • Symptoms: Small, pitted, blackhead-like areas; painful red lumps that increase in size and rupture; leaking abscesses; and scarring.
    • Stages (Hurley Staging):
      • Stage I (Mild): Single or isolated lumps without sinus tracts or scarring.
      • Stage II (Moderate): Recurring, separated lumps with some scarring and tunnel formation.
      • Stage III (Severe): Multiple interconnected tunnels and abscesses across a large area. 
    Causes and Risk Factors 
    • Causes: The exact cause is unknown, but it involves hair follicle blockage, which causes swelling and immune system overreaction.
    • Risk Factors: Primarily begins after puberty, often in the late teens or early 20s. Obesity and smoking are significant factors that can trigger or worsen the condition. It is more common in women and often has a genetic component. 
    Treatment and Management
    While there is no cure, treatments aim to manage flares and reduce pain: 
    • Medications: Topical or oral antibiotics (like clindamycin or tetracycline), painkillers (NSAIDs), hormonal therapies, and oral retinoids.
    • Biologics: Adalimumab or other TNF/IL-17 inhibitors can treat moderate-to-severe cases.
    • Procedures: Surgical drainage, laser hair removal, or, for severe cases, excision of the affected skin.
    • Lifestyle: Managing weight, smoking cessation, and using warm compresses. 
    It is important to see a dermatologist for early diagnosis, as delaying treatment can lead to worsening scarring and pain.
